title: Mosaic sex chromosome complement
clinical_history: A 16-year-old girl with short stature has two cell lines reported on constitutional blood karyotype. Use the ISCN string to interpret mosaicism. This case is nomenclature-focused and does not include a full cut-out karyotype.
plain_language_interpretation: Mosaicism with two cell lines: 12 cells are 45,X and 18 cells are 46,XX. A slash separates cell lines. Numbers in square brackets are clone sizes, not chromosome counts.
explanation: ISCN writes mosaicism by listing cell lines separated by a slash, conventionally with the abnormal line first when one line is normal, or by decreasing abnormality/clone size according to laboratory style. Clone sizes in square brackets count cells, not chromosomes. 45,X[12]/46,XX[18] means twelve 45,X cells and eighteen 46,XX cells. This mosaic complement is still classified with Turner syndrome clinically, but the ISCN must show both lines.
hints: A slash in ISCN separates cell lines (mosaicism), not chromosomes.
The number in square brackets is the number of cells in that clone, not the chromosome count.
Write each cell line with its own count and sex-chromosome complement.
